scene: Day 180, frozen river at a stone island mill under the ship's dark straight-edged slab, which fills the sky: the mill's sluice gate is open and white water bursts through the channel, breaking the ice into tilting slabs; where the water shows, the ring of pale light on the ice is broken and fading. Reed (blue-gray scarf) and Mara (purple forearm band) sit in a small wooden rowing boat in the black open water, a red fuel can tied behind it, Mara half standing and waving with both arms. On the ice nearby, the Worker (plain mint-headed alien, holding its flat silver case again) has turned back and raises one arm to wave, while the Surveyor (blue shoulder stripe) waits beside it. What makes it scary: the ship is leaving with one of them, and only the breaking ice let the two humans out.

Day 160, night inside the stone mill by the fireplace: the Worker (plain alien, no case, face gone gray, lying on its side under a brown wool blanket) is being fed by the Surveyor (mint-green head, blue shoulder stripe), who kneels beside it and holds out half of a small pale cube in its gloved fingers. Reed (blue-gray scarf) and Mara (purple forearm band) stand pressed against the stone wall in the foreground, wide-eyed, firelight on their faces, frost on the window behind them. What makes it scary: the alien that scanned them through walls for 160 days is inside their home, two feet away, and it is not looking at them at all.
